draft.title: Rome's legacy
card: A legacy is something a society leaves behind that later people keep using or building on. Ancient Rome left many legacies.
Buildings and roads
Romans built long, paved roads and aqueducts, which carried water to towns by channels and bridges. Many Roman roads and some aqueducts are still visible today.
Law and government

Roman law included ideas such as a person being innocent until proved guilty, and written laws open to all. Later societies drew on Roman ideas about government, such as elected officials and a senate.
Language
Romans spoke Latin. Many modern languages, such as Italian, French and Spanish, grew from Latin. English has also borrowed thousands of Latin words.
draft.remember: Rome's legacy is what later societies kept: roads, aqueducts, law, Latin and ideas about government.

a.q: Why is the Latin language part of Rome's legacy?
opts: Languages such as French and Spanish grew from it
Romans forced every country to speak it today
It is still the main language of Italy now
It was invented by the Senate to rule provinces
a.why: Latin is a legacy because later people kept using and building on it: French, Spanish and Italian grew from it. The claim that Italy speaks Latin is wrong, because Italians speak Italian, which developed from Latin.
a.clue: A legacy is something later people built on.

b.q: A town in modern Spain has a stone bridge that carries water channels, built by Romans nearly 2000 years ago. Which legacy of Rome does it show best?
opts: An aqueduct, which carried water to towns
A paved road, which linked distant towns
A Roman law, which was written for all
A Latin word, which later languages borrowed
b.why: A structure that carries water along channels on a bridge is an aqueduct. A road also links places, but it carries people and goods, not water.
b.clue: Think about what the bridge carries.

a.best: Languages such as French and Spanish grew from it

b.best: An aqueduct, which carried water to towns

problems.detail: The stem says the bridge 'carries water channels', and the right option is the only one that mentions water ('carried water to towns'). The clue 'Think about what the bridge carries' adds to this, so a student can match the word 'water' without knowing what an aqueduct is.

b.q: A Roman town in what is now Spain grew too big for its wells. Engineers found a fresh spring in the hills 15 km away. Which Roman structure would they build to supply the town?
opts: An aqueduct
A paved road
A senate house
A written law code
b.why: Aqueducts carried water to towns over long distances, using channels and bridges. A paved road also crossed long distances, but it carried people and goods, so it could not supply the town from the spring.
b.clue: Think about what each structure was built to carry.

a.best: Languages such as French and Spanish grew from it
